Multiply the base factor by the bounding box extent in each dimension to get the cell count [S1][S3, unofficial].

Source [S1] provides the formula $N_x = d_x * (lambda * N / V)^{1/3}$, where $d_x$ is the diagonal length (a measure of extent) and the term $(lambda * N / V)^{1/3}$ acts as a scaling factor derived from the base factor (lambda) and other scene properties. Source [S3] provides an identical formula structure $R_x = d_x * (lambda * N / V)^{1/3}$, explicitly defining $d_x$ as the extent of the bounding box. Both sources confirm that the number of cells (count) in a dimension is the product of the spatial extent ($d_x$) and a calculated factor involving the base parameter ($lambda$). Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
